newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI allows banks to buy shares from market.
newsitem.headline: India RBI allows banks to buy shares from market.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Saturday it has decided to allow banks to purchase shares and debentures in the secondary market.

"It has now been decided to allow banks to purchase shares and debentures in the secondary market within the existing ceiling of 5.0 percent of incremental deposits," RBI said as part of its monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).
It did not give details immediately.

Until now banks were only allowed to subscribe to shares or debentures in the primary market. Such investment was limited to 5.0 percent of the additional deposits that banks mobilise in the current year over the previous year.
